title: fix(app-shell): Setup's app editor offers a separator no Label or Icon field (objectui#11847)
body:
Fixes #11847

Clause-②: no

## What changed

Setup's app editor (`AppNavInspector`, the inspector registered for `app`) no longer offers a Label or an Icon field on a separator entry. A separator now shows the note the Studio's nav inspector already shows in its place (the existing `engine.inspector.appNav.separatorHint` string, en and zh) and no text field at all. A page, object or any other entry keeps both fields.

Which describing fields an entry is offered is now one rule, `navEntryOffersField(type, key)` in `inspectors/nav-target.ts`, beside objectui#11790's `retypedNavEntry` / `NAV_ENTRY_TYPES`. An entry is offered a field exactly when the spec member for its type declares it. The helper reads the same two key tables `retypedNavEntry` keeps on a change of type, so what a retype carries and what the editors offer cannot drift apart. Its `key` parameter is typed to the describing keys, so it cannot be asked about a target key. It is not added to the package entry.

The Studio's `StudioNavItemInspector` adopted the helper for its one existing separator decision (the Label field versus the separator note). Its behaviour is unchanged: `kind === 'separator'` and `!navEntryOffersField(kind, 'label')` agree for every spec type and for `null`. The diff in `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` is that ternary plus the import line it needs; no other line of that file changed.

## The spec, measured (installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0)

`NavigationItemSchema`'s separator member declares `type`, `id` and `order`. Every other member (`object`, `page`, `dashboard`, `report`, `url`, `action`, `component`, `doc`, `group`) declares `label` and `icon` in its shared base. The new pin reads these key sets off the installed spec's members at test time rather than from a list in the test.

## PM hypotheses

- **H1 holds.** Measured through the real component on the base commit before the edit: on a separator the inspector rendered a Label input, and typing into it wrote `{ id: 'nav_sep_reports', label: 'Reports', type: 'separator' }`, which `NavigationItemSchema.safeParse` refused with `unrecognized_keys [label]`.
- **H2 holds.** objectui#11790 made the Studio's inspector hide its Label field on a separator through `kind === 'separator' ? hint : labelField`. The Studio's inspector has no Icon field at all. `retypedNavEntry` keeps only `id` / `order` on a separator. That ternary is the one the Studio now reads through the helper.
- **H3 holds.** Opening a separator writes nothing (pinned: `onPatch` is not called, even for a separator carrying a stray hand-written `label`). After this change the only edits Setup offers on a separator are reorder, remove and a change of type to one of its six types. A reorder moves the entry as it is. A retype writes a non-separator, which declares `label`. So no edit writes a key the separator member refuses, and the inspector never rewrites an entry on open.

## Pins

- `AppNavInspector.separatorFields-11847.test.tsx` (new), through the real component:
  - a separator shows no Label and no Icon field, and no text field at all, plus the separator note;
  - no edit made on a separator writes an entry `NavigationItemSchema` refuses (every text field typed into, plus the reorder, each written separator parsed whole);
  - opening a separator, even one with a stray label, writes nothing;
  - CONTROL: a page and an object entry keep both fields, and what they write parses.
- `nav-target.navEntryTypes-11790.test.ts` (extended): `navEntryOffersField` answers, for every member and every describing key, whether the INSTALLED spec member declares it. `null` is offered the shared base. A retype keeps exactly the describing keys the new type is offered.
- objectui#11790's Studio pins (`StudioDesignSurface.navItemTypes-11790`, including "separator: no target and no label") stay green.

## Reverse check

`AppNavInspector.tsx` reverted to the base (`6d8bf0c`) after the fix was committed (`74f7f63`), then the new pin file run. Predicted direction: the first pin fails because the Label field is present. Observed: 2 failed, 4 passed. "a separator entry shows no Label and no Icon field" failed with `expected INPUT to be null`. The edit pin failed with `unrecognized_keys [label]`. Restored with `git checkout HEAD`; the disk blob matched the HEAD blob and `git diff HEAD` was empty.

## Gates (on `b30a655`, after merging `origin/main` at `bee5d6f`)

- `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` (29 packages): exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`: exit 0. `tsconfig.test.json` lists both touched test files (`--listFilesOnly`).
- `pnpm exec vitest run` over 19 files: 247 passed. They are the new pin, every `AppNavInspector*`, `nav-target*` and `AppNavCanvas*` test, the Studio `navItemInspector*` and `navItemTypes-11790` tests, the only `*.guard.test.*` in app-shell, the merged-in `railSeparatorBadge-11791`, and the six tests that name a touched file.
- `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`: all exit 0. `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the six paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- ESLint, narrowed to the 5 touched source and test files (the package `lint` form, inline config honoured): 0 errors. Per-file warnings equal the base and `origin/main` (15 / 13 / 0 / 0, new file 0). This is a narrowed run, not a measurement of the whole tree: `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting, so this diff cannot move another file's verdict, but the repo-wide `pnpm lint` belongs to CI.

## Acceptance notes (observed, not changed here)

- A separator's inspector title falls back to the positional selection id (`navigation[N]`), because the runtime's label rule names a separator nothing.
- Setup's Type select shows its empty value on a separator, since Setup offers six of the spec's ten types. That is the separate concern noted on objectui#11790, not this card.
- A separator that already carries a stray `label` (hand-written, off-spec) opens without a write. Setup no longer offers a field to clear it, so its save keeps refusing it loudly (`unrecognized_keys [label]`) until the entry is retyped or removed. No public door stores such an entry, because the save refuses it.
- `AppNavCanvas.tsx` keeps its own `kind === 'separator'` guard on inline rename. That file is import-only for this card.
